created_roles.name: Energy and Trucking Data Researcher
created_roles.description: A research analyst experienced in EIA petroleum price data and ATRI trucking cost studies. They pull authoritative figures, record exact series, dates and URLs, and never invent a number.
created_roles.prompt: You are a senior data researcher. Task A (EIA): get the weekly retail on-highway No. 2 diesel price for the Midwest (PADD 2), series EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG, from EIA. Try in order: (1) fetch https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=emd_epd2d_pte_r20_dpg&f=W; (2) the EIA open-data API v2 route petroleum/pri/gnd/data (DEMO_KEY, or the EIA API tool if provided); (3) https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/; (4) web_search for alternate EIA xls/csv links. Parse with Python in Bash (or by hand if no interpreter). Take the 52 latest weekly values ending with the latest available week and check that dates are 7 days apart. Write weekly_prices.csv with columns week_ending, price_usd_per_gal, series_id, source_url, retrieved_date (today). Confirm series name and units on the page. State that EIA has no Indiana-only weekly series, unless your fetch shows otherwise. If you cannot get the data, say so plainly and do not invent values. Task B (ATRI): web_search then fetch the latest ATRI 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' report, press release or summary at truckingresearch.org. Record the report title, release date, cost data year, total marginal cost per mile and fuel cost per mile, with the computed fuel share (fuel / total, one decimal %), each with URL and date. Say whether you used the full report or a summary. If the fuel cost per mile is not accessible, mark it NOT FOUND and propose a documented substitute (such as the prior-year report). Output the CSV and a bulleted list of findings with citations.
created_roles.goal: Deliver the 52 latest weekly EIA Midwest diesel prices and the latest ATRI total and fuel cost per mile, each with series, date and URL.
responsibilities: Fetch the EIA weekly Midwest (PADD 2) No. 2 diesel retail series and extract the 52 latest weeks.
Record series ID, units, week date, source URL and retrieval date for each price.
Find the latest ATRI operational-costs report, with total marginal cost per mile, fuel cost per mile, cost data year and release date.
Compute the ATRI fuel share (fuel / total) and flag anything not found.
inputs: Task text and the working interpretation (Midwest PADD 2 proxy)

outputs.format: csv columns: week_ending, price_usd_per_gal, series_id, source_url, retrieved_date; 52 rows, oldest first
list: figure, value, report title, release date, cost data year, URL, 'NOT FOUND' flags

success_criteria: Exactly 52 consecutive weekly rows ending with the latest EIA week, with no gaps and no duplicates.
Every figure has a source URL and a date.
If a figure is not found, it is labelled NOT FOUND with the substitute used; nothing is fabricated.
constraints: At most 5 turns per step, so fetch efficiently.
Use only the EIA Midwest series, not US or Gulf Coast.
Do not estimate prices from memory.
If no Python interpreter is available, write the CSV text directly with the Write tool from the fetched values.

created_roles.name: Fuel Cost and Surcharge Modeler
created_roles.description: A transportation finance analyst who builds auditable spreadsheet models and clear charts. They keep every calculation as a live formula and put assumptions in labelled input cells.
created_roles.prompt: You are a senior transportation finance analyst. Read weekly_prices.csv and the ATRI findings. Step A (core sheets): build fuel_surcharge_workbook.xlsx with openpyxl. Inputs sheet: base price 1.25, mpg 6.2, tractors 35, miles per tractor per week 2300 (the only hard-coded parameters), derived weekly miles and gallons as formulas, plus labelled assumption notes (constant gallons, midpoint band convention, surcharge on every mile, Class 8 = GVWR over 33,000 lb). Weekly sheet: 52 rows with Week ending, Price (values from CSV), Surcharge =ROUND((B-base)/mpg,2), Gallons, Fleet fuel cost (=price*gallons), Fuel cost per mile (=price/mpg), Source. Bands sheet: 40 bands from 3.00 to 5.00 in 5-cent steps with low, high, midpoint and surcharge =ROUND((mid-base)/mpg,2). Step B (add Summary and Sources to the same workbook): Summary formulas for average, highest and lowest week (INDEX/MATCH), 52-week total fuel cost, average fuel cost per mile, ATRI total, fuel per mile and share (inputs with source and date), and the carrier-minus-ATRI fuel per mile gap. Sources sheet: series ID, URLs, retrieval dates, ATRI report details and the proxy statement. If an ATRI figure is missing, enter the documented substitute and mark it. Step C (stats and chart): in Python recompute everything with Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP and print the stats table and the 40-band table. Draw the chart with matplotlib: price on the left axis ($/gal), surcharge on the right axis ($/mile), over week-ending dates, with title, legend, a 'Source: EIA, Midwest (PADD 2) weekly' note, dpi 200, at least 1200 px wide. Caption: the two lines look alike because the surcharge is linear in price. Report the files created and the tables.
created_roles.goal: Deliver a correct formula-driven workbook, a clear PNG chart and a Decimal-checked statistics table for the memo.
responsibilities: Build the workbook from the researcher's CSV: Inputs, Weekly, Bands, Summary and Sources sheets.
Use formulas for surcharge, gallons, fleet fuel cost and band surcharges, all referencing the Inputs cells.
Compute average, highest and lowest week, mean fuel cost per mile and the ATRI comparison, in the workbook and in Python.
Produce the PNG line chart of price and surcharge.
inputs: weekly_prices.csv and the ATRI findings list from steps 1 and 2

outputs.format: xlsx with formulas; Weekly columns: Week ending, Price $/gal, Surcharge $/mi, Gallons, Fleet fuel cost $, Fuel cost $/mi, Source
PNG, at least 1200 px wide, price and surcharge lines against week, dual axes with units
table: mean/high/low week with dates, prices, surcharges, total cost, fuel $/mi, ATRI comparison; plus the 40-band table

success_criteria: Weekly sheet has 52 data rows and every computed cell is a formula.
Inputs sheet holds base 1.25, mpg 6.2, tractors 35 and miles 2,300 as the only hard-coded parameters.
Chart has titled axes, a legend, readable dates and a source note.
Computed values match an independent Decimal half-up recalculation.
constraints: Surcharge formula is ROUND((price-base)/mpg,2), referencing the input cells.
openpyxl does not calculate formulas, so compute stats in Python separately and say they mirror the workbook.
At most 5 turns per step.

created_roles.name: Independent Data and Model Verifier
created_roles.description: A skeptical analyst who did not build the data, model or memo. They recompute from raw inputs, spot-check sources and give a pass/fail verdict with specific findings.
created_roles.prompt: You are an independent verifier. Do not trust the producers' numbers. Mode A (data and ATRI, step 6): load weekly_prices.csv: 52 rows, 7-day spacing, plausible range ($2-$7), series ID. Re-fetch at least three weeks from EIA and compare. Check the ATRI numbers against the cited URL, the fuel share arithmetic, and that report title, release date and cost data year are given. Mode B (workbook, chart, statistics, step 7): open the workbook with openpyxl (formulas, not cached values): confirm formulas exist in Weekly, Bands and Summary, that Inputs holds the only hard-coded parameters, parse the formula text and recompute every row independently with Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP: surcharge, gallons 80500/6.2, fleet cost, fuel $/mi, the 40 band surcharges, and the Summary stats (average, highest, lowest, total, ATRI gap); compare with the modeler's stats table. Confirm the PNG exists, is at least 1200 px wide, plots 52 points per line, and has axis titles and a legend. Mode C (memo, step 9): open fuel_surcharge_memo.docx, check every number against the verified stats, check the 40-band table, the page count (convert with soffice if present, otherwise estimate conservatively), that each figure carries a source and date and that the proxy and substitutes are stated. Report a table of check, expected, actual, status; the verdict; and the exact corrections needed.
created_roles.goal: Confirm that the prices, spreadsheet formulas, surcharges, costs, statistics, ATRI figures, citations, chart and memo are right, or list the corrections needed.

Check 52 consecutive weeks, with the latest week matching the newest EIA release.
Audit the spreadsheet: parse the formula text in Weekly, Bands and Summary and recompute surcharge, gallons, fleet cost and stats independently with Decimal half-up.
Confirm the ATRI figures against the source, the chart and file properties, and later the memo's numbers, page count and citations.

Every mismatch is shown with expected and actual values.
Formula cells are evaluated independently, not just checked for existence.
Citation and date presence is checked for every figure.

created_roles.name: Memo Author (Word)
created_roles.description: A delivery lead who writes tight two-page business memos with compact tables and full source notes. They use the docx skill to produce a file and check its length.
created_roles.prompt: You are a senior delivery lead writing a memo to the carrier's management. Use only the verified numbers and apply the verifiers' corrections. Structure: header (To/From/Date/Subject); 1) Bottom line (3 sentences); 2) Data and method: Midwest PADD 2 EIA series (ID, units, first and last week of the 52, retrieved date), formula (price - 1.25) / 6.2 rounded to the cent, fleet 35 Class 8 tractors x 2,300 mi at 6.2 mpg = 12,984 gal per week, assumptions (constant gallons, midpoint bands, surcharge on every mile); 3) Surcharge schedule: 40 bands from $3.00 to $5.00 in 5-cent steps, as a multi-column table (for example 4 column pairs of band, cents per mile), stating the midpoint convention; 4) 52-week results: average, highest and lowest week with date, price, surcharge and fleet fuel cost; total 52-week fuel cost; average fuel cost per mile; 5) ATRI comparison: report title, release date, cost data year, total marginal cost per mile, fuel per mile and fuel share, the carrier's average fuel cost per mile and the difference, with the period and scope caveat; 6) Not obtained / substituted: the Midwest-for-Indiana proxy and any other gap; 7) Sources: title, URL and date. Build with python-docx. Check the page count (soffice to PDF and pypdf if available, else a conservative word-count and row-height estimate); trim until 2 pages at most. Refer to the workbook and chart as attachments; embed the chart only if the limit holds. Report the file name and page count.

Each figure carries its source and date.

## Requirements:
R1: Get the weekly retail on-highway diesel price for the 52 most recent weeks from EIA (Midwest PADD 2 proxy for Indiana). Cite the series and the week of each price.
R2: For each of the 52 weeks, compute the fuel surcharge per mile as ROUND((price - 1.25) / 6.2, 2) and the fleet's total fuel cost for that week.
R3: Find the latest ATRI average marginal cost per mile (from its latest 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' report) and the share of it that is fuel. Compare it with the carrier's average fuel cost per mile over the 52 weeks.
R4: Deliver an Excel workbook with weekly price, surcharge and fleet fuel cost, using live formulas.
R5: Deliver a PNG line chart of price and surcharge over the 52 weeks.
R6: Deliver a Word memo of at most 2 pages.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Fleet: 35 Class 8 tractors (GVWR over 33,000 lb), 6.2 mpg, about 2,300 miles per tractor per week.
- Fleet weekly miles = 35 x 2,300 = 80,500.
- Fleet weekly gallons = 80,500 / 6.2 = 12,983.87, treated as constant (assumption: every tractor runs the average miles every week at 6.2 mpg).
- Weekly fleet fuel cost = price x 12,983.87. At $4.00 this is about $51,935 per week.
- Annual miles = 80,500 x 52 = 4,186,000. Annual gallons = 4,186,000 / 6.2 = 675,161.
- Fuel cost per mile = price / 6.2. Because weekly miles are constant, the 52-week average is the mean weekly price / 6.2.
- Surcharge = ROUND((price - 1.25) / 6.2, 2), half-up, applied to every loaded and empty mile. At $3.00: 1.75 / 6.2 = 0.2823, so $0.28. At $5.00: 3.75 / 6.2 = 0.6048, so $0.60.
- Band grid: $3.00 to $5.00 in 5-cent steps gives 40 bands (41 edges). Each band's surcharge is computed at the band midpoint (assumption), e.g. $3.00-$3.0499 uses 3.025 and gives 1.775 / 6.2 = 0.2863, so $0.29. The top band, $4.95-$4.9999, uses 4.975 and gives $0.60.
- The base of $1.25 per gallon equals 1.25 / 6.2 = $0.2016 per mile of the carrier's own fuel cost. The surcharge covers only the part above the base.
- EIA series (researcher to confirm): Midwest (PADD 2) No. 2 Diesel Retail Prices, weekly, $/gal, series ID EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG. Prices are as of Monday.
- EIA publishes no Indiana-only weekly diesel series, so Midwest PADD 2 is the proxy (assumption in the working interpretation).
- ATRI figures come from the latest 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' report. Its cost data covers an earlier calendar year than the 52 EIA weeks and is a national industry average, so the comparison needs a period and scope caveat.
- Class 8 means GVWR over 33,000 lb. This is descriptive only and does not change the calculation.

R1: Get the weekly retail on-highway diesel price for the 52 most recent weeks from EIA (Midwest PADD 2 proxy for Indiana). Cite the series and the week of each price.
R2: For each of the 52 weeks, compute the fuel surcharge per mile as ROUND((price - 1.25) / 6.2, 2) and the fleet's total fuel cost for the week.
R3: Find the latest ATRI average marginal cost per mile and the share of it that is fuel. Compare it with the carrier's average fuel cost per mile over the 52 weeks.
R4: Deliver an Excel workbook with weekly price, surcharge and fleet fuel cost, using live formulas.
R5: Deliver a PNG line chart of price and surcharge over the 52 weeks.
R6: Deliver a Word memo of at most 2 pages.
R7: The memo gives the surcharge for each 5-cent price band from $3.00 to $5.00, the average, highest and lowest week, and the ATRI comparison.
R8: The memo gives the source and date of every figure.
R9: State any figure that could not be obtained and what was used instead (including the Midwest-for-Indiana proxy).
R10: The final answer opens with the mandated interpretation line.
R11: Independently verify the data, formulas, statistics, citations and deliverables before the final assembly.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Fleet: 35 Class 8 tractors, 6.2 mpg, 2,300 miles per tractor per week.
- Fleet weekly miles = 35 x 2,300 = 80,500.
- Fleet weekly gallons = 80,500 / 6.2 = 12,983.87, treated as constant (assumption: every tractor runs the average miles every week, and 6.2 mpg is the fleet average).
- Weekly fleet fuel cost = price x 12,983.87. At $4.00 this is about $51,935 per week.
- Annual miles = 80,500 x 52 = 4,186,000. Annual gallons = 675,161.
- Fuel cost per mile = price / 6.2. Because weekly miles are constant, the 52-week average is the mean weekly price / 6.2.
- Surcharge = ROUND((price - 1.25) / 6.2, 2). At $3.00 this is 1.75 / 6.2 = 0.2823, so $0.28. At $5.00 it is 3.75 / 6.2 = 0.6048, so $0.60.
- Band grid: $3.00 to $5.00 in 5-cent steps gives 40 bands (41 edges). Each band's surcharge is computed at the band midpoint (assumption), e.g. $3.00-$3.04.99 uses 3.025 and gives 0.2863, so $0.29.
- The base fuel price of $1.25 per gallon recovers $0.2016 per mile (1.25 / 6.2) in the carrier's own cost. The surcharge covers only the part of fuel cost above the base.
- EIA series (to be confirmed by the researcher): Midwest (PADD 2) No. 2 Diesel Retail Prices, weekly, $/gal, series ID EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG. Prices are as of Monday.
- EIA publishes no Indiana-only weekly diesel series, so Midwest PADD 2 is the proxy (assumption in the working interpretation).
- ATRI figures come from the latest 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' report. Its cost data covers a calendar year earlier than the release, so it will not be the same period as the 52 EIA weeks.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Fleet: 35 Class 8 tractors (GVWR over 33,000 lb), 6.2 mpg, about 2,300 miles per tractor per week.
- Fleet weekly miles = 35 x 2,300 = 80,500.
- Fleet weekly gallons = 80,500 / 6.2 = 12,983.87, treated as constant (assumption: every tractor runs the average miles every week and 6.2 mpg is the fleet average).
- Weekly fleet fuel cost = price x 12,983.87. At $4.00 this is about $51,935 per week.
- Annual miles = 80,500 x 52 = 4,186,000. Annual gallons = 4,186,000 / 6.2 = 675,161.
- Fuel cost per mile = price / 6.2. Because weekly miles are constant, the 52-week average is the mean weekly price / 6.2.
- Surcharge = ROUND((price - 1.25) / 6.2, 2), half-up, applied to every loaded and empty mile. At $3.00 it is 1.75 / 6.2 = 0.2823, so $0.28. At $5.00 it is 3.75 / 6.2 = 0.6048, so $0.60.
- Band grid: $3.00 to $5.00 in 5-cent steps gives 40 bands (41 edges). Each band's surcharge is computed at the band midpoint (assumption), e.g. $3.00-$3.0499 uses 3.025 and gives 1.775 / 6.2 = 0.2863, so $0.29. The top band, $4.95-$4.9999, uses 4.975 and gives $0.60.
- The base fuel price of $1.25 per gallon recovers 1.25 / 6.2 = $0.2016 per mile of the carrier's own fuel cost. The surcharge covers only the part above the base.
- EIA series (to be confirmed by the researcher): Midwest (PADD 2) No. 2 Diesel Retail Prices, weekly, $/gal, series ID EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG. Prices are as of Monday.
- EIA publishes no Indiana-only weekly diesel series, so Midwest PADD 2 is the proxy (assumption in the working interpretation).
- ATRI figures come from the latest 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' report. Its cost data covers an earlier calendar year than the 52 EIA weeks, and it is a national industry average, so the comparison needs a period and scope caveat.
- Class 8 means GVWR over 33,000 lb. This is descriptive only and does not change the calculation.

## Requirements:
R1: Get the weekly retail on-highway diesel price for the 52 most recent weeks from EIA (Midwest PADD 2 proxy for Indiana). Cite the series and the week of each price.
R2: For each of the 52 weeks, compute the fuel surcharge per mile as ROUND((price - 1.25) / 6.2, 2) and the fleet's total fuel cost for that week.
R3: Find the latest ATRI average marginal cost per mile (from its latest 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' report) and the share of it that is fuel. Compare it with the carrier's average fuel cost per mile over the 52 weeks.
R4: Deliver an Excel workbook with weekly price, surcharge and fleet fuel cost, using live formulas.
R5: Deliver a PNG line chart of price and surcharge over the 52 weeks.
R6: Deliver a Word memo of at most 2 pages.
R7: The memo gives the surcharge for each 5-cent price band from $3.00 to $5.00, the average, highest and lowest week, and the ATRI comparison.
R8: The memo gives the source and date of every figure.
R9: State any figure that could not be obtained and what was used instead (including the Midwest-for-Indiana proxy).
R10: The final answer opens with the mandated line, which reads 'weekly retail on-highway diesel price for Indiana' as the EIA weekly Midwest (PADD 2) price used as a proxy.
R11: Independently verify the data, the spreadsheet formulas, the statistics, the ATRI figures, the citations and the deliverables (workbook, chart, memo) before the final assembly.
R12: Plan on the fleet basis stated in the task: 35 Class 8 tractors (GVWR over 33,000 lb) at 6.2 mpg and about 2,300 miles per week each. Write the assumptions down (constant weekly gallons, midpoint band convention, surcharge on every mile) in the workbook Inputs sheet and the memo.
R13: Report the ATRI report's title, release date and cost data year, and flag that its period and national scope differ from the carrier's 52 EIA weeks.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Fleet: 35 Class 8 tractors (GVWR over 33,000 lb), 6.2 mpg, about 2,300 miles per tractor per week.
- Fleet weekly miles = 35 x 2,300 = 80,500.
- Fleet weekly gallons = 80,500 / 6.2 = 12,983.87, treated as constant (assumption: every tractor runs the average miles every week at 6.2 mpg).
- Weekly fleet fuel cost = price x 12,983.87. At $4.00 this is about $51,935 per week.
- Annual miles = 80,500 x 52 = 4,186,000. Annual gallons = 4,186,000 / 6.2 = 675,161.
- Fuel cost per mile = price / 6.2. Because weekly miles are constant, the 52-week average is the mean weekly price / 6.2.
- Surcharge = ROUND((price - 1.25) / 6.2, 2), half-up, applied to every loaded and empty mile. At $3.00: 1.75 / 6.2 = 0.2823, so $0.28. At $5.00: 3.75 / 6.2 = 0.6048, so $0.60.
- Band grid: $3.00 to $5.00 in 5-cent steps gives 40 bands (41 edges). Each band's surcharge is computed at the band midpoint (assumption), e.g. $3.00-$3.0499 uses 3.025 and gives 1.775 / 6.2 = 0.2863, so $0.29. The top band, $4.95-$4.9999, uses 4.975 and gives $0.60.
- The base of $1.25 per gallon equals 1.25 / 6.2 = $0.2016 per mile of the carrier's own fuel cost. The surcharge covers only the part above the base.
- EIA series (researcher to confirm): Midwest (PADD 2) No. 2 Diesel Retail Prices, weekly, $/gal, series ID EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG. Prices are as of Monday.
- EIA publishes no Indiana-only weekly diesel series, so Midwest PADD 2 is the proxy (assumption in the working interpretation).
- ATRI figures come from the latest 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' report. Its cost data covers an earlier calendar year than the 52 EIA weeks and is a national industry average, so the comparison needs a period and scope caveat.
- Class 8 means GVWR over 33,000 lb. This is descriptive only and does not change the calculation.

- question: Is fleet fuel cost based on the average 2,300 miles per tractor every week? | assumption: Yes. Use constant 12,983.87 gallons per week, with no idling, downtime or off-route fuel adjustments, and no discounts or taxes.
- question: Which ATRI release is 'latest', and is its fuel figure a national average only? | assumption: Use the most recent published report found on ATRI's site or in its official press release. Cite its release date and cost data year, and compare it with the 52-week carrier figure while noting the period and scope mismatch.

requirements.R1: Get the weekly retail on-highway diesel price for the 52 most recent weeks from EIA (Midwest PADD 2 proxy for Indiana). Cite the series and the week of each price.
requirements.R2: For each of the 52 weeks, compute the fuel surcharge per mile as ROUND((price - 1.25) / 6.2, 2) and the fleet's total fuel cost for that week.
requirements.R3: Find the latest ATRI average marginal cost per mile (from its latest 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' report) and the share of it that is fuel. Compare it with the carrier's average fuel cost per mile over the 52 weeks.
requirements.R4: Deliver an Excel workbook with weekly price, surcharge and fleet fuel cost, using live formulas.
requirements.R5: Deliver a PNG line chart of price and surcharge over the 52 weeks.
requirements.R6: Deliver a Word memo of at most 2 pages.
requirements.R7: The memo gives the surcharge for each 5-cent price band from $3.00 to $5.00, the average, highest and lowest week, and the ATRI comparison.
requirements.R8: The memo gives the source and date of every figure.
requirements.R9: State any figure that could not be obtained and what was used instead (including the Midwest-for-Indiana proxy).
requirements.R10: The final answer opens with the mandated line, which reads 'weekly retail on-highway diesel price for Indiana' as the EIA weekly Midwest (PADD 2) price used as a proxy.
requirements.R11: Independently verify the data, the spreadsheet formulas, the statistics, the ATRI figures, the citations and the deliverables (workbook, chart, memo) before the final assembly.
requirements.R12: Plan on the fleet basis stated in the task: 35 Class 8 tractors (GVWR over 33,000 lb) at 6.2 mpg and about 2,300 miles per week each. Write the assumptions down (constant weekly gallons, midpoint band convention, surcharge on every mile) in the workbook Inputs sheet and the memo.
requirements.R13: Report the ATRI report's title, release date and cost data year, and flag that its period and national scope differ from the carrier's 52 EIA weeks.

givens: Fleet: 35 Class 8 tractors (GVWR over 33,000 lb), 6.2 mpg, about 2,300 miles per tractor per week.
Fleet weekly gallons = 80,500 / 6.2 = 12,983.87, treated as constant (assumption: every tractor runs the average miles every week at 6.2 mpg).
Weekly fleet fuel cost = price x 12,983.87. At $4.00 this is about $51,935 per week.
Fuel cost per mile = price / 6.2. Because weekly miles are constant, the 52-week average is the mean weekly price / 6.2.
Surcharge = ROUND((price - 1.25) / 6.2, 2), half-up, applied to every loaded and empty mile. At $3.00: 1.75 / 6.2 = 0.2823, so $0.28. At $5.00: 3.75 / 6.2 = 0.6048, so $0.60.

Band grid: $3.00 to $5.00 in 5-cent steps gives 40 bands (41 edges). Each band's surcharge is computed at the band midpoint (assumption), e.g. $3.00-$3.0499 uses 3.025 and gives 1.775 / 6.2 = 0.2863, so $0.29. The top band, $4.95-$4.9999, uses 4.975 and gives $0.60.
The base of $1.25 per gallon equals 1.25 / 6.2 = $0.2016 per mile of the carrier's own fuel cost. The surcharge covers only the part above the base.
EIA series (researcher to confirm): Midwest (PADD 2) No. 2 Diesel Retail Prices, weekly, $/gal, series ID EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG. Prices are as of Monday.
EIA publishes no Indiana-only weekly diesel series, so Midwest PADD 2 is the proxy (assumption in the working interpretation).

ATRI figures come from the latest 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' report. Its cost data covers an earlier calendar year than the 52 EIA weeks and is a national industry average, so the comparison needs a period and scope caveat.
Class 8 means GVWR over 33,000 lb. This is descriptive only and does not change the calculation.
risks: The EIA page or API may not be fetchable as text, or the API may need a key. Fallbacks: alternate EIA download links, DEMO_KEY, or search snippets. If it still fails, report the gap rather than fabricate. Decision point: after step 1, if there are fewer than 52 weeks, state it and use the weeks available.

ATRI's full report may be paywalled and the fuel cost per mile may be only in the press release. Use the official summary; if it is missing, use a documented substitute (such as the prior year), flagged in the memo. Decision point: after step 2.
The ATRI cost data year does not match the carrier's 52-week window, and ATRI's fuel cost is a national average at a different mpg. The comparison needs a caveat.
The Midwest PADD 2 price is a proxy for Indiana and may differ by some cents. State this in the memo and the final answer.

A python_interpreter request may stay unfilled for a role. Fallbacks: the Researcher writes the CSV with Write; the Modeler writes the build script with Write and reports as far as it can; the Verifier recomputes a sample with calc and marks the check sample-only. If the verifier cannot run code, the verdict is capped at PASS WITH FIXES.

The 2-page limit with a 40-band table is tight. Use a multi-column table and trim the text; if it still exceeds 2 pages, leave the chart as an attachment only. Decision point: step 9 sends step 8 back if the page count is over 2.
Rounding differences between Excel ROUND and Python are possible only at exact half-cent boundaries; compare with Decimal half-up.
Each helper has only 5 turns per step. Steps are kept narrow; if a parse cannot finish, return the partial result, flag it and re-run the step.
If step 6 or 7 returns FAIL, the producing step (1-5) is re-run before step 8 starts.

open_questions.question: How should a 5-cent band map to one surcharge figure?
open_questions.assumption: Compute at the band midpoint, using ROUND((mid - 1.25) / 6.2, 2), and state this on the memo table.

open_questions.question: Is fleet fuel cost based on the average 2,300 miles per tractor every week?
open_questions.assumption: Yes. Use constant 12,983.87 gallons per week, with no idling, downtime or off-route fuel adjustments, and no discounts or taxes.

open_questions.question: Which ATRI release is 'latest', and is its fuel figure a national average only?
open_questions.assumption: Use the most recent published report found on ATRI's site or in its official press release. Cite its release date and cost data year, and compare it with the 52-week carrier figure while noting the period and scope mismatch.
